events.text:
**Pick: St. Joseph (about 3), with Grand Haven as the safer fallback. Every report is old, so my ratings are expectations rather than facts.**

| Port | My rating | Newest report |
|---|---|---|
| St. Joseph | 3 (good) | 2024-07-10, 20 days old |
| South Haven | 2 (average) | 2024-07-10, 20 days old |
| Grand Haven | 2 (average, lower end) | 2024-07-24, 6 days old |
| Muskegon | 2 (average) | 2024-07-10, 20 days old |

**What the reports say (2024)**
- **St. Joseph:**
  - The latest report was "very good fishing", rated 4. It was Chinook with coho and steelhead mixed in, mostly on spoons, in 80–90 ft of water (St. Joseph, 2024-07-10).
  - The weeks before were weaker: 1 on 07-03 after a sharp surface drop, with few boats out and a few coho and steelhead around 100 ft (St. Joseph, 2024-07-03). Before that it was 2 on 06-26 and 1 on 06-20, with spoons in about 100 ft (St. Joseph, 2024-06-26 and 2024-06-20).
- **South Haven:**
  - It was rated 2 on 07-10: a mixed bag of coho and Chinook on rotators and flies. The best depths were 75–80 ft and 105–110 ft of water (South Haven, 2024-07-10).
  - It was rated 3 on 07-03 in 90–110 ft (South Haven, 2024-07-03).
- **Grand Haven (freshest data):**
  - Chinook were caught 35–100 ft down in 60–120 ft of water, along with a few steelhead and coho. Green and orange spoons and white flasher flies worked. Coho were rated 1, Chinook were not rated, and "a few salmon" came on green meat rigs and glow plugs (Grand Haven, 2024-07-24).
  - On 07-10 it was rated 2, with 40–100 ft down in 65–120 ft of water. Meat rigs "worked very well" (Grand Haven, 2024-07-10).
  - On 07-03 it was rated 3 for Chinook (Grand Haven, 2024-07-03).
- **Muskegon:**
  - It was rated 2 on 07-10: salmon 40–100 ft down in 70–120 ft of water, on meat rigs and flasher flies (Muskegon, 2024-07-10).
  - It was slow to average in June (Muskegon, 2024-06-20 and 2024-06-26).

**Water now.** The buoys show a weekly average surface temperature of about 73 F at St. Joseph, 71 F at South Haven and 68 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon. Each is up about 1–2 F over the week (get_current_conditions, week before 2024-07-30). Live data, the modeled cold-layer depth and the wind forecast were unavailable, so I can't judge wave conditions. Check the marine forecast before you go.

**History at this time of year (not this year)**
- Late July to early August 2023 had Muskegon rated 2–3 and Grand Haven rated 2–3. Fish were 50–100 ft down in 80–160 ft of water (Muskegon, 2023-08-09; Grand Haven, 2023-08-09; Muskegon, 2023-08-02; Grand Haven, 2023-08-02).
- South Haven was a steady 2 in 2023. In 2022 it was 1 (South Haven, 2023-08-02, 2023-07-26 and 2022-08-03).
- St. Joseph was good on 2023-07-26, with most fish around 120 ft. After a sharp surface-temperature drop in the week of 2023-08-09 it went to 1, with boats trolling around the pierheads (St. Joseph, 2023-07-26 and 2023-08-09). In 2022 it was 1 (St. Joseph, 2022-07-20).

**My read**
- I'd expect St. Joseph to be the best of the four if the 07-10 bite held. It was the only port rated excellent, and its surface water is the warmest. Its results swing a lot from week to week, though, and its report is the oldest, so I'd call it a 3 rather than a 4.
- I'd expect Grand Haven and Muskegon to be steady and average. Grand Haven's 07-24 report was a step down from earlier in July, and Muskegon's 2022–2023 history is good for early August.
- I'd expect South Haven to be average, with rotators and flies in 75–110 ft of water.
